entities.rationale: The objects are the welcome modal, the activation task, prototype variants and matched participants. These are exactly the proposal components, flows and study participants the onboarding product manager already decomposes and tests.

relations.rationale: The link is a candidate causal contribution of one feature to abandonment at a funnel step. Attributing drop-off to a specific screen or element is the ordinary relation in funnel and usability analysis.

processes.rationale: Removal followed by observed change in completion is ordinary staged-variant comparison. Framing restoration-and-recurrence as a distinct confirmatory process is a mild extension, but it is still a feature toggle across prototype builds and does not reorganize how change is understood.

operations.rationale: Disabling a modal in an otherwise fixed prototype and comparing completion is routine. Deliberately restoring it in a counterbalanced trial to check recurrence adds a second toggle step that a usability practitioner can run without new tooling or design skills, so it is accommodated rather than reinterpreted.

observables.rationale: Evidence is task completion and abandonment counts across variants, plus observed participant behavior. These are the prototype task completion and funnel events already listed as ordinary evidence.

inferences.rationale: The licensed conclusion is a bounded, feature-specific causal contribution to activation failure that leaves other dependencies open. Prioritizing one change from a small experiment while withholding claims about the rest is the baseline's ordinary output.

failure_modes.rationale: Learning effects across repeated tasks, participant differences, concurrent prototype changes and spontaneous variation are the standard confounds a usability-study practitioner already guards against with matching and counterbalancing.

rationale: Stripping the pharmacovigilance vocabulary leaves a feature-toggle prototype study: disable the modal, measure activation completion, re-enable it and check whether drop-off returns. The baseline practitioner already runs staged variants and small experiments with prototypes, reads funnel completion as evidence and prioritizes single changes from those results. Nothing in the mapping asks them to inspect a new kind of object, treat a new signal as evidence or draw a conclusion type they would not ordinarily draw. The explicit rechallenge step is the only addition, and it is a second ordinary variant comparison rather than a reorganization of inquiry.

epistemic_changes.practitioner_actions: The practitioner builds two otherwise identical prototypes with the modal on and off and runs matched participants through activation. The mapping adds only an explicit restore-and-recheck pass, ideally counterbalanced, which is a repeat of the same comparison in the opposite direction.
epistemic_changes.noticed_features: Attention stays on completion versus abandonment at the modal step and on observed participant hesitation or errors there. No new class of feature becomes salient; the mapping simply asks the practitioner to watch for recurrence after restoration as well as improvement after removal.
epistemic_changes.evidential_warrants: Support rests on completion differences between variants, strengthened when abandonment returns on restoration. This is the same warrant as any staged-variant comparison, with the reversal serving as replication rather than a foreign evidential standard.
epistemic_changes.next_inquiry: The practitioner still moves on to the remaining redesign elements one at a time and to interaction effects the single-toggle design cannot resolve. The mapping explicitly leaves those dependencies open, matching the baseline's ordinary iterative prioritization.

most_consequential_baseline_difference: The only material difference is treating deliberate reintroduction of the removed element as a required confirmatory step. Ordinary practice would often stop after the removal comparison, so the mapping slightly raises the bar for calling the modal causal, but it does not change what is inspected, measured or concluded.
uncertainty: Baseline scope is an authored hypothesis; some onboarding product managers rely mainly on interviews and funnel analytics and rarely run controlled on/off prototype comparisons, which would push the mapping toward Adjacent.

Whether counterbalanced within-subject restoration is routine for this practitioner is unclear; if their usability work is purely between-group or qualitative, the rechallenge step is a stronger extension than assessed here.
The mapping's single-feature toggle does not address the interaction part of the target question, but that is a matter of scope coverage, not displacement, and was not scored.
